subject: Agriculture
title: The Cold Chain
description: A fast breakdown of The Cold Chain for builders.

hook.text: Without refrigeration, half of all perishable food would rot before reaching consumers. Cold is invisible infrastructure.

buildup.text: The cold chain—refrigerated trucks, warehouses, and ships—keeps food safe from farm to fork.

discovery.text: In India, 40% of fresh produce spoils due to cold chain gaps. That's $14 billion of food rotting annually.

twist.text: Building cold chains in hot developing countries requires massive energy—often fossil fuels. Cooling food warms the planet.

climax.text: Solar-powered cold rooms are emerging in rural Africa and India, offering clean cooling without grid electricity.

punchline.text: The poorest countries lose the most food. Cold is a luxury they can't afford—yet.

quiz.question: How much fresh produce spoils in India due to cold chain gaps?
